etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English porcioun, borrowed from Old French porcion, from Latin portio (“a share, part, portion, relation, proportion”), akin to pars (“part”); see part. Compare proportion.

definitions.definition: That which is divided off or separated, as a part from a whole; a separated part of anything.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Luke 12:46, columns 2–1:
quote.text: The Lord of that ſeruant  […]  will appoint him his portion with the vnbeleeuers.

quote.citation: 1827, [John Keble], The Christian Year: Thoughts in Verse for the Sundays and Holydays throughout the Year, volume (please specify |volume=I or II), Oxford, Oxfordshire:  […]  [B]y W. Baxter, for J. Parker; and C[harles] and J[ohn] Rivington, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Man's portion is to die and rise again.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XVII, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume III, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 146:
quote.text: "Everywhere the same!" exclaimed Francesca, as she resumed her seat—"the same human misery—the same human portion!...

definitions.definition: The part of an estate given or falling to a child or heir; an inheritance.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Luke 15:12, column 1:
quote.text: Father, giue me the portion of goods that falleth to me.

quote.citation: 1829, Edgar Allan Poe, “Tamerlane”, in Al Aaraaf, Tamerlane and Minor Poems:
quote.text: O! yearning heart! I did inheritThy withering portion with the fame,The searing glory which hath shoneAmid the jewels of my throne,Halo of Hell!

quote.citation: 1613–1614 (date written), John Fletcher, William Shak[e]speare, The Two Noble Kinsmen: […], London:  […]  Tho[mas] Cotes, for Iohn Waterson;  […], published 1634, →OCLC, Act V, scene iv, page 85:
quote.text: Commend me to her, and to piece her portion / Tender her this.

quote.citation: 1726 October 28, [Jonathan Swift], Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.  […]  [Gulliver’s Travels], volume I, London:  […]  Benj[amin] Motte, […], →OCLC, part I (A Voyage to Lilliput):
quote.text: I took part of a small house in the Old Jewry; and being advised to alter my condition, I married Mrs. Mary Burton, second daughter to Mr. Edmund Burton, hosier, in Newgate-street, with whom I received four hundred pounds for a portion.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To divide into amounts, as for allocation to specific purposes.
(transitive) To endow with a portion or inheritance.

quote.text: Him portioned maids, apprenticed orphans, blest.

pronunciation: Scotland, Ireland, other varieties without the horse–hoarse merger
